summary: The Petitioner, JSW Hydro Energy Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Petitioner) has filed this petition for recovery of unrecovered energy charges due to a shortfall in energy generation for reasons beyond the control of the generating station during the FY 201819 in respect of Karcham Wangtoo HEP, seeking the following relief(s): - c) Pass any such further order(s) which this Hon'ble Commission may deem just fit and proper in favour of the Petitioner. _52. In view of the above deliberations, the Commission is of the view that energy shortfall of 152.80 MU is for the reasons beyond control of the Petitioner and accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for the corresponding energy charge shortfall as given below:_ 4. The said order of the Commission was appealed against by the Respondent, PSPCL, in Appeal No. 13 of 2022 before APTEL. The APTEL, by the judgment dated 2.4.2025 in the above appeal, and the said judgment has remanded Petition No. 184/MP/2019 by referring to the Commission's following orders: _"24. It is evident from perusal of these orders that the shortfall in saleable schedule energy in these three cases also pertains to the controlled period of tariff Regulations, 2019 and accordingly, 14(6) (7) & (8) of these Regulations were invoked and discussed. We further note that in the order dated 26th May, 2023 passed in petition No. 550/MP/2020, the Commission has referred to the order dated 4th February, 2020 in Petition No. 184/MP/2019 which is the order impugned in the instant appeal, but on some other context. Therefore, it cannot be said, as argued on behalf of the 2nd Respondent, that the order impugned in this appeal had not been brought to the notice of the Commission at the time of passing the above subsequent orders._ _25. It is further argued on behalf of the 2nd Respondent that these three subsequent orders of the Commission are not binding on this Tribunal and cannot be treated as precedents to be followed by this Tribunal. It cannot be gain said that the orders of the Commission are not binding upon this Tribunal. Having said that, we are constrained to note that an adjudicatory forum like the Electricity Regulatory Commission is not only expected but also required to be consistent and uniform in its approach in order to avoid regulatory uncertainty. Even after referring to the order impugned in this appeal, the Commission took a contrary view in order dated 26th May, 2023 passed in Petition No. 550/MP/2020 as well as the two subsequent orders without explaining any reason to deviate from the view taken in the order dated 4th February, 2020 which has been challenged in this appeal. In case, according to the Commission, the interpretation given to Regulation 44(6) of 2019 Tariff Regulations in the subsequent three orders dated 26.05.2023, 26.09.2023 and 01.01.2024 is correct, then the order dated 04.02.2020 which has been assailed in this appeal also needs a relook._ _26. Having regard to such inconsistent approach adopted by the Commission, we are of the view that the case at hand requires reconsideration by the Commission. The impugned order as such, cannot be sustained. The same is hereby set aside. The appeals stands allowed._ _27._ **_The case is remanded back to the Commission for fresh consideration in line with its subsequent orders dated 26th May, 2023, 26th September, 2023 and 1st January, 2024 passed by the Commission in Petition Nos. 550/MP/2020, 98/MP/2022 and 464/MP/2019 respectively._** 7. The Respondent no. 6, PSPCL, in its reply dated 28.7.2025, has submitted that the Commission, in its order dated 12.02.2019 (Petition No. 205/MP/2018), held that beneficiaries such as PSPCL have the first right of refusal for overload capacity. PSPCL exercised this right but did not schedule the overload capacity, which was instead scheduled by Haryana Discoms. Consequently, PSPCL did not pay capacity charges for the unused overload. JSW Hydro’s Petition No. 439/MP/2019, seeking clarification on the order dated 12.2.2019 in Petition No. 205/MP/2018, was dismissed on 30.06.2021, affirming the finality of the first right of refusal. Subsequently, JSW Hydro filed Petition No. 184/MP/2019 to recover shortfall charges for FY 2018-19, which was allowed by order dated 04.02.2020 and appealed by PSPCL. 10. Before proceeding further, it is pertinent to note that the Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 21.08.2025, submitted that there was an error in the calculations annexed to its written submissions dated 13.06.2025, relating to the computation of the amount to be payable by the Respondent, PSPCL. The Petitioner requested that the shortfall in energy generation be considered as 116.83 MUs and that the total recoverable amount be Rs. 2036.30 lakh. The Petitioner further requested that the recoverable amount be apportioned among the four beneficiaries in accordance with the Commission’s earlier orders and that a final order be passed directing the necessary adjustments. 11. In view of the above, since the Petitioner has revised the calculations and the same have also been submitted by the Respondent, PSPCL, the comments of the parties on the methodology of the claim have not been considered in this order. It is further clarified that the scope of the remand is limited to the adjustment of energy accounted for under DSM, and this is dealt with in the following paragraphs. 13. Accordingly, in compliance with the APTEL order dated 02.04.2025 in appeal no. 13 of 2022 the para 50,51,52 and 53 of the order dated 4.2.2020 in petition no. 184/MP/2019 are revised as under: _52. In view of the above deliberations, the Commission is of the view that energy shortfall of 116.83 MUs is for the reasons beyond control of the Petitioner and accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for the corresponding energy charge shortfall as given below:_ 14. In view of the above, the Petitioner is directed to refund the differential amount
title: Petition under Regulation 44(6), (7) & (8) of The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 for recovery of unrecovered energy charges due to shortfall in energy generation for reasons beyond the control of the generating station during the FY 2018-19 in respect of Karcham Wangtoo HEP. JSW Hydro Energy Ltd. Corrigendum Order date: 18.05.2026
